plan.focus: What a mild day after a fog streak does to someone who has been wintering inside — and what it lets the rest of the city overlook.
plan.why: Four straight cycles of fog and overcast, then this. The weather is the most democratic thing in Oakland — everyone gets the same sky. But not everyone gets the same response to it. One person on the record stayed in. The mayor's office is moving money and deadlines. The council president is suspicious of comfort. The mild day is the connective tissue between all of it.

plan.interpretation: The weather is a mood ring for the city. A mild day after a fog streak doesn't just change the temperature — it changes what people feel entitled to ask for. The man who stayed inside through the winter and the council president who distrusts comfort are the same story: the weather tells us what we can bear, and what we can bear shapes what we demand.
